website_verified_via: Linked in Wilson's pamphlet statement (Book 4, p. 41): www.WilsonForSpringfield.com

bio.statement: Wilson's pamphlet statement lists his occupation as financial advisor at LPL Financial.

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet, General Election Nov. 3, 2026 (Book 4, p. 41)

bio.statement: He lists past work as a technician at Les Schwab, technician/parts at Papé Group and banker at Pacific Continental Bank.

bio.statement: He lists no prior governmental experience.

bio.statement: Wilson describes himself as a sixth-generation Oregonian and father of three who grew up around Lane County build sites, auto shops and baseball fields.
bio.excerpt: I am a sixth-generation Oregonian and proud father of three who grew up at Lane County build sites, auto shops, and baseball fields.

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet, General Election Nov. 3, 2026 (Book 4, p. 41)

bio.statement: The Portland Tribune describes Wilson as a wealth adviser and the Republican nominee for the Springfield seat.
bio.excerpt: And Springfield City Councilor Kori Rodley is running as a Democrat against Republican Adam Wilson, a wealth adviser, for Lively’s seat.

source.publisher: Portland Tribune

positions.statement: Wilson says he would reduce regulatory building costs and stop out-of-state investment firms from buying local homes.
positions.excerpt: HOUSING: Reduce regulatory building costs and keep single-family homes for working class families by stopping out-of-state investment firms from buying up local homes.

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet, General Election Nov. 3, 2026 (Book 4, p. 41)

positions.statement: Wilson says tax dollars should be spent wisely before the state asks for more money.
positions.excerpt: ACCOUNTABILITY: Ensure our tax dollars are spent wisely fixing roads, keeping us safe, improving K-12 education, and making government work for residents before the state ever asks for more money.

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet, General Election Nov. 3, 2026 (Book 4, p. 41)

positions.statement: Wilson says data centers should bring their own power, pay their fair share and stay out of communities that do not want them.
positions.excerpt: DATA CENTERS: Require big corporations to bring their own power, pay their fair share, stay out of communities that do not want them, and ensure local families do not pay higher utilities.

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet, General Election Nov. 3, 2026 (Book 4, p. 41)

positions.statement: Wilson lists career and technical education and the unemployment system as jobs priorities.
positions.excerpt: JOBS: Prioritize Career and Technical Education and fix our broken unemployment system.

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet, General Election Nov. 3, 2026 (Book 4, p. 41)

positions.statement: Wilson says he would repeal House Bill 3115 so Springfield can clear homeless camps.
positions.excerpt: HOMELESSNESS & DRUG ABUSE: Repeal House Bill 3115 to restore local control so Springfield can clear homeless camps.

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet, General Election Nov. 3, 2026 (Book 4, p. 41)

positions.statement: Wilson says he would serve no more than two terms.
positions.excerpt: No more career politicians. If elected, I will serve no more than two terms in office.

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet, General Election Nov. 3, 2026 (Book 4, p. 41)
